key_insight: Indoor photovoltaics paired with (anti)ferroelectric energy storage and low-power computing could enable autonomous edge AI nodes that reduce reliance on centralized servers.
engineering_relevance: Reliable indoor edge AI requires co-designing light harvesting, energy storage and computation to match local energy availability with device demand.
method: Assess indoor photovoltaic requirements for distributed intelligence.
Discuss emerging photovoltaic materials and remaining performance gaps.
Explore (anti)ferroelectrics for electrostatic storage and in-memory neuromorphic computing.
evidence_signal: The abstract presents a perspective on material opportunities and system requirements, without reporting quantitative benchmarks or an integrated device demonstration.
watch_item: Reliable operation remains contingent on matching variable indoor energy supply to storage capacity and computational demand.
paper_title: Computing at the Edge Enabled by Indoor Photovoltaics and Ferroelectrics
